clue.text: Second time senior grabs European lottery win?

indicators.note: to grab something is to take hold of it, so one piece closes around another

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a very short time
T is the standard abbreviation for time
Sr is the abbreviation for senior
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A pensioner's second lucky draw brings a European jackpot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' is a brief moment, not an ordinal. A motser is Australian slang for a large sum of money, especially one won by gambling.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian slang for a big pile of cash, typically a gambling windfall, so a lottery jackpot is an example; the question mark flags that.

clue.text: Owner in Florida raising plantation crop

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising something lifts it so it reads from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: Assam tea is grown on Indian plantations

explanation.surface: A Florida landowner is growing a plantation crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Owner in Florida' looks like scene-setting but is the whole definition: the word is old Southern US dialect for a slave-owning master.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical dialect form of master used in the American South, where plantation slaves addressed the property holder this way.

clue.text: Cry for sweet trike tractor mangled

indicators.note: something mangled is crushed out of shape, so the letters are wrenched into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A child wails for candy after a tractor flattens their tricycle.
explanation.walkthrough: The twelve letters of the two vehicles rearrange into the Halloween phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Children call this phrase at doors on Halloween to demand candy, so it is literally a call made to get confectionery.

clue.text: Caught leaving, scoffing at gatecrashing

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so that letter is taken out of the word

blocks.note: c is the cricket abbreviation for caught
to scoff at someone is to scorn them

explanation.surface: Someone caught as they leave was sneering at uninvited guests.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the C from SCORNING. Sorning is a Scots word for forcing yourself on others for free board and lodging.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots term for imposing yourself on someone's hospitality uninvited, sponging bed and food, much like turning up unasked at a party.

clue.text: Tip about independent girl

indicators.note: about here means around, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: the tip of something is its end
I is the abbreviation for independent

explanation.surface: A word of advice about a self-reliant young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' reads as advice but means the end of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is a female first name, and crosswords routinely define given names by the word girl or boy.

clue.text: Mix of white and brown filling the cruet

indicators.note: a filling sits inside something, so the letters are found within the words that follow

blocks.note: found in thE CRUet

explanation.surface: Salt and pepper mixed together in the cruet set.
explanation.walkthrough: The white and brown suggest salt and pepper in a cruet, but they are the colour being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale greyish-yellow or beige shade, the colour of unbleached linen, which sits between white and light brown.

clue.text: Number in church left after pleasant Sunday afternoon Mass

indicators.note: after says one piece follows the other in reading order

blocks.note: PSA is the abbreviation for a pleasant Sunday afternoon, an old chapel gathering
L is the abbreviation for left
m is the abbreviation for mass

explanation.surface: A churchgoer stays behind after a lovely Sunday afternoon Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: Mass looks like the church service but supplies M, the physics abbreviation. 'Number' is something sung, not a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred song from the biblical book sung in services, and a musical item is often called a number.

clue.text: With knife around, are ready in Tonga

indicators.note: around says one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: a panga is a broad African machete
an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated a

explanation.surface: Armed with knives, the islanders of Tonga are prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is not prepared but cash: ready money. 'are' is not the verb but the metric unit.
explanation.definitionFit: The pa'anga is the currency of Tonga, and ready is British slang for cash available to spend.

clue.text: European in bad cabin mishap heading each way?

indicators.note: something gone bad is spoilt and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A European traveller suffers an accident in a cabin and is unsure which way to go.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes in among the letters of the cabin mishap and all twelve are rearranged. The amphisbaena is a mythical serpent with a head at each end.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes something like the fabled two-headed serpent, which has a head at both ends and so faces both directions.

clue.text: Don’t get up with sloth — tons hide until spring?

blocks.note: to lie in is to stay in bed
W is the abbreviation for with
the ai is the three-toed sloth
T is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: Stay in bed lazily, like heavy animals hibernating until the spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'until spring' suggests winter hibernation, but spring is the pounce of an ambusher.
explanation.definitionFit: To lurk concealed ready to ambush is to stay hidden until the moment to leap out and attack.

clue.text: Malay tribesman collecting wings of pinkish butterfly

indicators.note: the wings of something are its two sides, so only the outside letters are kept
to collect is to gather in, so one piece takes the other inside it

blocks.note: the Moros are Muslim Malay peoples of the southern Philippines
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A tribesman in Malaysia catches a pinkish butterfly.
explanation.walkthrough: The butterfly in the surface is the definition, while 'pinkish' only donates its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A genus of large tropical American butterflies famous for iridescent blue wings.

clue.text: As a high priest deployed oil and arcana

indicators.note: deployed means spread out and arranged, so the letters are set out anew

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A high priest makes use of holy oil and secret mysteries.
explanation.walkthrough: Aaron, brother of Moses, was the first high priest of Israel; the adjective derived from his name means priestly.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to Aaron, the first Hebrew high priest, so it means pertaining to or befitting such a pontiff.

clue.text: Medium small nag about one animal hunter

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a rip is a worthless old horse
the Roman numeral for one
a trapper catches animals for their fur

explanation.surface: A middling pony circling an animal hunter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medium' looks like a size to go with small, but it is a person who contacts the dead. 'nag' is a horse, not a scold.
explanation.definitionFit: A psychic who claims to receive knocking messages from the dead at seances is a kind of spiritualist go-between.

clue.text: Cheated grasping landlord out of new money once

indicators.note: grasping says the first piece holds on to the next, so they are joined end to end
out of means without, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: to do someone is to swindle them
Peter Rachman was a notorious exploitative London slum landlord of the 1950s
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A greedy landlord fiddled his tenants out of fresh cash in years gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: Rachman, a byword in Britain for slum landlords, loses N. The didrachma was an ancient Greek silver coin worth two drachmas.
explanation.definitionFit: An old Greek silver coin of two drachmas, so it is a former currency unit no longer in circulation.

clue.text: Condition in convent beginning to niggle — move out of place?

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that letter is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
to unship is to remove something, such as an oar, from its fixed position

explanation.surface: A nun's minor irritation in the convent makes her want to relocate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Condition' means status or state, as in the suffix -ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of being a nun, formed like friendship or kingship, is the status of a woman living in a convent.

clue.text: Inner parts of nose lacking straight bits of hair

indicators.note: lacking means without, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: the passages inside the nose
str is the abbreviation for straight

explanation.surface: The inside of the nose lacks any straight hairs.
explanation.walkthrough: Nose hair is a red herring: the hair here is wool or animal fibre combed in spinning.
explanation.definitionFit: Short fibres combed out from wool or silk before spinning are the waste fragments of animal hair.

clue.text: Martial art youngster breaking into a triumphant cry

indicators.note: to break into something is to get inside it, so one piece enters the other

blocks.note: a kid is a child
taken as written
io is a Greek-derived shout of triumph

explanation.surface: A youngster in a martial arts class breaks a board with a victorious yell.
explanation.walkthrough: A and IO together make the outer shell. Io is a classical exclamation of triumph or joy.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese self-defence discipline using throws and locks, one of the established fighting systems of Asia.

clue.text: Bird soaring around a village

indicators.note: in a down entry, soaring goes upward, so the word reads from bottom to top
around says one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: the lark is a songbird
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird flies high over a village.
explanation.walkthrough: The lark is turned upward, then A slips inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A southern African word for a native settlement of huts enclosed by a fence, so it names a rural community.

clue.text: At home during quiet function

indicators.note: during means within a span, so one piece is set inside the other

blocks.note: sh is a call for quiet
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: Staying in during a quiet social event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'function' looks like a party but is mathematical: sinh is the hyperbolic sine.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyperbolic sine is a standard mathematical operation, written as this abbreviation on calculators.

clue.text: Edible Aralia — national dish of Japan

blocks.note: udo is a Japanese aralia whose shoots are eaten
N is the abbreviation for national

explanation.surface: An edible plant forms Japan's national dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'national dish' reads as a phrase, but national gives N and the definition is the following words.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick wheat-flour noodles served in broth are a staple Japanese meal.

clue.text: Constellation endlessly absorbing independent physicist

indicators.note: without an end, the last letter is dropped
to absorb is to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: Draco, the Dragon, is a northern constellation
I is the abbreviation for independent

explanation.surface: A star group absorbs a lone scientist forever.
explanation.walkthrough: Draco loses its last letter, then takes I in. Paul Dirac was the British quantum physicist.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Dirac, Nobel laureate who predicted antimatter, was a pioneer of quantum mechanics.

clue.text: Gaudy South African bird eating contents of gourd

indicators.note: the contents are what lies inside, so the outer letters are discarded
to eat is to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: the coly, or mousebird, is an African bird
the inside letters of the word

explanation.surface: A flashy African bird pecks at the inside of a gourd.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird in the surface is the outer piece, and 'Gaudy' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal adjective meaning richly or showily coloured, close in sense to flashy or garish.

clue.text: Camel’s wild spirit

indicators.note: something wild is unruly and out of control, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the possessive supplies the extra letter

explanation.surface: The camel has an untamed temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' looks like the animal's nature but is a drink; the apostrophe in the first word is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mexican distilled liquor made from agave, so it is an alcoholic spirit like tequila.

clue.text: One foolish foreign knight avoiding active duty

indicators.note: avoiding means keeping clear of, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: Sir Galahad is the purest of the Round Table knights
AD is the abbreviation for active duty

explanation.surface: A foolish foreign knight dodges military service.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the first three words: a galah is an Australian cockatoo and, by extension, Australian slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian slang for a fool, taken from the noisy pink-and-grey cockatoo, so a silly person from abroad.

clue.text: Antiquarian ignoring Roman figure in reconstruction of Avebury

indicators.note: ignoring something leaves it out, so that letter is dropped
a reconstruction rebuilds something in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: V is the Roman numeral five
taken as written

explanation.surface: A historian disregards Roman remains when rebuilding the Avebury stones.
explanation.walkthrough: Avebury is a prehistoric stone circle in Wiltshire; John Aubrey was the seventeenth-century antiquarian who first recorded it, so the clue fits its answer.
explanation.definitionFit: John Aubrey, the seventeenth-century English writer of Brief Lives, was a pioneering student of ancient monuments.

clue.text: Objection to a new port

blocks.note: ob is an old abbreviation for objection, as in obs and sols
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Residents oppose building a new harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Oban is a ferry port on the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A west Highland harbour town that serves as the gateway for ferries to the Hebridean islands.

clue.text: Way of dying, beheaded easily in Tudor times

indicators.note: to behead is to cut off the top, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: a manner of death, as in a gruesome death

explanation.surface: Beheading was an easy way to die under the Tudors.
explanation.walkthrough: Execution in Tudor England is a nice scene, but 'beheaded' only removes a letter. Eath is an obsolete word for easy or easily.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb used by Spenser and his contemporaries meaning without difficulty.

clue.text: A good nursemaid protecting Latin goddess

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround and shield it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: taken as written
G is the abbreviation for good
an aia (ayah) is a nursemaid in India
L is the abbreviation for Latin

explanation.surface: A kind nanny watches over a classical goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: A, G and AIA together form the shell around L. Aglaia was one of the three Graces of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Aglaia, the Grace of splendour, is one of the three minor deities attending Aphrodite.

clue.text: A western fish well known up north

blocks.note: taken as written
W is the abbreviation for western
the eel is a long snake-like fish

explanation.surface: A fish from the west is famous in the north of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well known' looks like famous, but the definition is the word well as it is said in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scots interjection meaning well then, used to introduce a remark, so it is the northern form of the filler.

clue.text: Plagiarise cutting wit, mostly of writers

indicators.note: something cutting into another goes inside it
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: to crib is to copy someone else's work
Attic salt is refined wit, so salt means wit

explanation.surface: Writers mostly copy each other's sharp jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: Salt means wit through the phrase Attic salt, the refined humour of ancient Athens; 'cutting' looks like sharp but tells one piece to go inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective from scribe, so relating to clerks or copyists who write out texts.

clue.text: Poet’s short song

indicators.note: cut short means the final letter is lopped off

blocks.note: An English comic poet, so the poet's name with its possessive S

explanation.surface: A poet writes a brief little song.
explanation.walkthrough: Pam Ayres is a popular British writer of humorous verse; her name plus the possessive, docked of its last letter, gives the old spelling of air.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic spelling of air, meaning a melody or a lute song of the Elizabethan period.

clue.text: Galatians importing old Roman pillar

indicators.note: to import is to bring in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: Gal is the abbreviation for the Epistle to the Galatians
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: St Paul's letter to the Galatians brings in an ancient Roman column.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is not a target in sport but the turning post in a Roman chariot circus.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman circus the meta, a turning post at each end of the track, was called the goal in English.

clue.text: In the past, applaud and exaggerate sweet spirit

blocks.note: an obsolete verb meaning to cheer or cherish
to bounce once meant to boast or overstate

explanation.surface: People once cheered and hyped a sugary liqueur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the past' belongs to the first piece, marking an obsolete sense, not a time setting for the whole clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetened liqueur made by steeping cherries in brandy or rum, so a sugary alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Larvae all over warm and dry land area in Ecuador

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other
all over can mean turned over completely, so the whole lot reads backwards

blocks.note: to air laundry is to warm and dry it
an acre is a measure of land
EC is the international vehicle code for Ecuador

explanation.surface: Larvae swarm over the hot, arid land of Ecuador.
explanation.walkthrough: 'warm and dry' reads as climate, but it is what you do when airing laundry. Cercariae are the tadpole-like larvae of parasitic flukes.
explanation.definitionFit: Free-swimming juvenile stage of trematode flatworms, so they are a type of grub.

clue.text: Tall and thin papilionaceous plant rush mostly concealed

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
what is concealed is hidden from view, so those letters disappear

blocks.note: Lathyrus is the sweet pea genus, with butterfly-shaped flowers
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lanky pea plant hides among the rushes.
explanation.walkthrough: Papilionaceous means butterfly-like, the shape of pea flowers. RUSH loses its last letter, and the remaining three vanish from the plant name.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect word meaning lath-like: long, lanky and slender, like a thin strip of wood.

clue.text: Element isolated from strongly colloidal compound

indicators.note: something isolated from a mixture is extracted out of it, so the letters are lifted from inside

blocks.note: found in stronGLY COLloidal

explanation.surface: A chemist separates an element from a thick colloidal mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: The chemistry surface makes 'Element' look like the answer, but the answer is a compound; an element of the words is the run of letters taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: A diol such as ethylene glycol, used in antifreeze, is a chemical substance made of several bonded elements.
